questions.q: Based on site of infection, infection of the bone and medullary cavity is called:
questions.exp: Osteomyelitis: bone & medullary cavity; m/c location: metaphysis of long bone. (Book p137)

questions.q: Most common location of osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: m/c location: metaphysis of long bone. (Book p137)

questions.q: Infection involving the joint is called:
questions.exp: Septic arthritis: joint. (Book p137)

questions.q: Most common etiology of infections of the skeletal system:
questions.exp: Bacteria (m/c): pyogenic organisms and TB. (Book p137)

questions.q: Local reaction in pyogenic organisms is:
questions.exp: Pyogenic organisms: severe local/periosteal reaction. (Book p137)

questions.q: Local reaction in tuberculosis of bone:
questions.exp: TB: limited local reaction (↓inflammatory reaction). (Book p137)

questions.q: TB of short bones (hand & foot) produces:
questions.exp: TB of short bones (hand & foot) → severe local reaction. (Book p137)

questions.q: Osteomyelitis is common in young children or elderly population due to:
questions.exp: In young children or elderly population d/t relatively low immunity. (Book p137)

questions.q: Most common route/source of osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Hematogenous (m/c): from pre-existing infection. (Book p137)

questions.q: Puncture wounds cause osteomyelitis by which route?
opts: Direct - contaminated source in direct contact with bone
questions.exp: Direct (eg puncture wounds) & post-surgical (iatrogenic): contaminated source in direct contact with bone. (Book p137)

questions.q: Post-surgical (iatrogenic) osteomyelitis is classified under:
questions.exp: Post surgical (iatrogenic): contaminated source in direct contact with bone - direct route. (Book p137)

questions.q: In septic arthritis, osteomyelitis develops when infection spreads from:
questions.exp: Septic arthritis: joint → (infection) → bone. (Book p137)

questions.q: Most common organism infecting the musculoskeletal system:
questions.exp: Staphylococcus aureus: m/c organism infecting musculoskeletal system. (Book p137)

questions.q: Staphylococcus aureus is the m/c cause of:
questions.exp: m/c cause of: osteomyelitis overall, acute osteomyelitis, chronic osteomyelitis. (Book p137)

questions.q: Staphylococcus aureus is the m/c cause of osteomyelitis in all of the following except:
opts: Sickle cell disease with metaphyseal involvement is NOT due to it - it is excepted; others are developed countries
questions.exp: m/c in developed countries, developing countries, immunocompromised (HIV/AIDS), open fracture, post surgical; in sickle cell with metaphysis involvement it is still Staph, diaphyseal is Salmonella. (Book p137-138)

questions.q: Osteomyelitis in a sickle cell disease patient is most commonly caused by:
questions.exp: Sickle cell disease: Salmonella → diaphyseal involvement. (Book p138)

questions.q: In sickle cell disease, if the metaphysis is involved, the organism is:
questions.exp: Sickle cell: Salmonella (diaphyseal); if metaphysis involved: Staphylococcus aureus. (Book p138)

questions.q: Osteomyelitis in IV drug abusers is caused by:
questions.exp: IV drug abusers: Pseudomonas. (Book p138)

questions.q: Organism causing osteomyelitis following animal bite:
questions.exp: Following animal bite: Pasteurella. (Book p138)

questions.q: Organism causing osteomyelitis following human bite:
questions.exp: Following human bite: Eikenella. (Book p138)

questions.q: Prolonged parenteral therapy leads to osteomyelitis by:
questions.exp: Prolonged parenteral therapy: fungal organisms. (Book p138)

questions.q: Most common site of osteomyelitis in infants and children:
questions.exp: Overall/infant/children: femur (distal > proximal) > tibia. (Book p138)

questions.q: Most common site of osteomyelitis in adults:
questions.exp: Adult: vertebrae. (Book p138)

questions.q: Reasons for metaphyseal involvement in osteomyelitis include all except:
opts: Most vascular region of bone (increased nutrition for organism)
Hair pin loop arrangement of blood vessels
questions.exp: Reasons: most vascular region (↑nutrition), hair pin loop arrangement → sluggish blood flow (easy exit to bone), few monocytes & macrophages (↓protection). (Book p138)

questions.q: Hair pin loop arrangement of metaphyseal blood vessels causes:
opts: Sluggish blood flow - easy exit of organism to bone
questions.exp: Hair pin loop arrangement → sluggish blood flow (easy exit to bone). (Book p138)

questions.q: In acute osteomyelitis, the organism reaches the metaphysis within:
questions.exp: Organism reaches metaphysis <24 hours → systemic manifestations: fever, pain. (Book p138)

questions.q: Systemic manifestations of acute osteomyelitis appear along with:
questions.exp: Organism reaches metaphysis <24 hours: systemic manifestations - fever, pain. (Book p138)

questions.q: Abscess in acute osteomyelitis is formed:
questions.exp: Abscess formed: after 24 hours. (Book p138)

questions.q: Sequestrum is:
opts: Dead bone formed inside the abscess
questions.exp: Sequestrum (dead bone) formed inside abscess. (Book p138)

questions.q: Involucrum is:
opts: New bone formed due to periosteal reaction that contains the spread
questions.exp: Involucrum: new bone that contains the spread (d/t periosteal reaction). (Book p138)

questions.q: Periosteal reaction (involucrum) on X-ray appears by about:
questions.exp: Periosteal reaction: ~10 days. (Book p138)

questions.q: Cloaca is defined as:
questions.exp: Cloaca: break in involucrum through which pus escapes. (Book p138)

questions.q: Sinus in chronic osteomyelitis is:
opts: Break in the skin through which pus drains out
questions.exp: Sinus: break in skin; cloaca + sinus → pus drains out. (Book p138)

questions.q: A young child with acute osteomyelitis presents with:
opts: High grade fever, pain & swelling, pseudoparalysis
Low grade fever with night sweats only
questions.exp: Young child: high grade fever, pain & swelling, pseudoparalysis. (Book p139)

questions.q: Pseudoparalysis in acute osteomyelitis means:
opts: Patient doesn't move the limb due to pain
questions.exp: Pseudoparalysis: patient doesn't move limb d/t pain. (Book p139)

questions.q: Causes of pseudoparalysis in a child include:
questions.exp: Causes of pseudoparalysis: septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, scurvy. (Book p139)

questions.q: In scurvy, pseudoparalysis occurs due to:
questions.exp: Scurvy (vit C deficiency): subperiosteal hemorrhage → pain → pseudoparalysis. (Book p139)

questions.q: Clinical hallmark of acute osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Acute: clinical hallmark not specific (fever & pain); chronic: sinus. (Book p139)

questions.q: Clinical hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Chronic osteomyelitis: clinical hallmark is sinus. (Book p139)

questions.q: Pathological hallmark of acute osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Acute: pathological hallmark abscess; chronic: sequestrum. (Book p139)

questions.q: Pathological hallmark of chronic osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Chronic osteomyelitis: pathological hallmark sequestrum. (Book p139)

questions.q: Blood culture in acute osteomyelitis is positive in:
questions.exp: Blood culture: 50% +ve. (Book p139)

questions.q: WBC/neutrophil, ESR and CRP in acute osteomyelitis are:
questions.exp: WBC/neutrophil, ESR, CRP: high, not specific. (Book p139)

questions.q: Sensitive & specific blood marker for acute osteomyelitis and septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Serum procalcitonin: sensitive & specific marker for acute osteomyelitis and septic arthritis. (Book p139)

questions.q: Investigation that picks up the earliest changes (within 24 hrs of onset) in osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: MRI: picks up earliest changes within 24 hrs of disease onset - marrow edema. (Book p139)

questions.q: Isotopes used in bone scan for osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Bone scan: technetium 99, gallium 67, indium 111 labelled WBC - accumulation in infection. (Book p139)

questions.q: X-ray changes in acute osteomyelitis are detected:
questions.exp: X-ray: changes detected after 24 hours of disease onset. (Book p139)

questions.q: Earliest X-ray change (within 48 hours) of acute osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Earliest X-ray change (within 48 hours): soft tissue lucency/shadow around bone. (Book p139)

questions.q: Earliest bony change on X-ray (7-10 days/2 weeks) in osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Earliest bony changes on X-ray (7-10 days/2 weeks): periosteal reaction. (Book p139)

questions.q: Gold standard investigation of osteomyelitis:
opts: Biopsy - tissue sample from site of infection
questions.exp: Biopsy: gold standard; tissue sample collected from site of infection. (Book p140)

questions.q: Definitive treatment of acute osteomyelitis presenting within 24 hours:
questions.exp: Presents within 24 hours: antibiotics ± drain the abscess. (Book p140)

questions.q: Definitive treatment of acute osteomyelitis presenting after 24 hours:
questions.exp: Presents after 24 hours: antibiotics + drain the abscess. (Book p140)

questions.q: Supportive treatment of acute osteomyelitis includes:
opts: Initial broad spectrum antibiotics, analgesics, antipyretics, rest & splint, icepack & elevation
questions.exp: Supportive: initial broad spectrum antibiotics, analgesics (pain), antipyretics (fever), rest & splint to prevent movement (↓pain), icepack & limb elevation (swelling). (Book p140)

questions.q: Total antibiotic duration in acute osteomyelitis:
opts: 6 weeks - 2 weeks IV followed by 4 weeks PO
questions.exp: 6 weeks: 2 weeks IV → 4 weeks PO. (Book p140)

questions.q: Long antibiotic duration in osteomyelitis is required due to:
opts: Low penetration of drug in bone
questions.exp: Long duration d/t low penetration of drug in bone; response assessed using CRP measurements. (Book p140)

questions.q: Response to antibiotic therapy in osteomyelitis is assessed using:
questions.exp: Response assessed using CRP measurements. (Book p140)

questions.q: Most common complication of acute osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Complications: chronic osteomyelitis (m/c). (Book p140)

questions.q: Spread of acute osteomyelitis to joint (septic arthritis) is prevented by:
questions.exp: Septic arthritis: bone → joint; prevented by growth plate. (Book p140)

questions.q: Septic arthritis as a complication of osteomyelitis is common in:
opts: <1 year - before growth plate formation; adults after growth plate fusion
questions.exp: Common in: <1 yr (before growth plate formation) and adults (after growth plate fusion). (Book p140)

questions.q: Other complications of acute osteomyelitis besides chronic osteomyelitis and septic arthritis:
questions.exp: Complications: chronic OM (m/c), septic arthritis, septicemia, growth disturbance. (Book p140)

questions.q: Duration of acute osteomyelitis:
questions.exp: Duration: acute <2 weeks; subacute 2-4 weeks; chronic >4 weeks. (Book p140)

questions.q: Subacute osteomyelitis lasts:
questions.exp: Subacute: 2-4 weeks. (Book p140)

questions.q: Chronic osteomyelitis is defined as infection lasting:
questions.exp: Chronic: >4 weeks following infection. (Book p140)

questions.q: Chronic osteomyelitis is:
opts: A de novo infection without acute phase
Always blood borne from distant focus
questions.exp: Chronic OM: sequelae/complication of acute osteomyelitis; >4 weeks following infection; clinical hallmark: sinus. (Book p140)
